al_new_wall_aka_kurt_russell_block.blurb: A compact sport wall tucked a short walk beyond the Sun Wall trail at Sand Rock, the sandstone ledge above Leesburg in Cherokee County. The wall is low, roughly 35 feet, and holds around seventeen bolted lines. Difficulty runs from an easy beginner pitch up to the low 5.11s, but the bulk of the routes cluster in the 5.10 range, with a handful of 5.7 to 5.9 options for warming up. It sees plenty of sun through the day and is sheltered from wind, which makes it a pleasant pick for cold winter days. Expect short, straightforward sport pitches rather than long endurance climbs.

al_the_zero_gravity_wall.blurb: A cliff band in the Southeast Section of Buck's Pocket, in northeast Alabama, found below the park overlook. It mixes bolted sport lines with trad and top-rope options across about sixteen routes. Grades run from the high 5.7 range to the low 5.12s, and the heart of the wall sits around 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate-to-hard leads more than beginners. Development here is still going on, so expect some loose or unfinished sections and treat the cliff with caution. Anchors and fresh lines may continue to appear over time.

al_spirit_area.blurb: A boulder cluster inside the Horse Pens 40 boulderfield near Steele in St. Clair County, reached by following the path a short way beyond the Mulletino block. This is straight sandstone bouldering with about eighteen problems, a good spread for mixed groups: a quarter of them are VB to V0, several land in the V3 to V5 band, and a lone problem near V7 caps it off. Horse Pens 40 is known for sloper-heavy, rounded features, and this spot fits that mold. It sits alongside neighboring boulders such as The Wash, so you can combine it with a longer circuit.

al_skywalker_area.blurb: Part of the central section of the Horse Pens 40 boulderfield in St. Clair County, near Steele, Alabama. Sixteen sandstone problems are logged here, making it a mid-sized stop on a bouldering circuit. The mix is weighted toward the easy and middle grades, with a good number of VB to V0 warm-ups and a cluster around V4, then a short tail of hard problems stretching into the V8 to V9 range. That spread lets a group with mixed abilities share one spot. Fall and winter are the favored seasons across the park.

al_mulletino_boulder.blurb: A well-known block in the front part of Horse Pens 40, the sandstone boulderfield outside Steele in St. Clair County, Alabama. Around sixteen problems and variations are packed onto and around it, ranging from easy VB and V0 moves through a solid middle of V3 to V6 and on to a few very hard lines in the V8 to V10 range. That breadth makes it a good place to spend a session whether you are warming up or projecting. The sandstone here is known for slopers and rounded holds, and cooler months give the best friction.
